column5: src/server/handlers.ts checks only stats.size against MAX_FILE_SIZE_BYTES before calling readFile; src/utils/fileUtils.ts implements these helpers with fs.promises.stat and an unbounded fs.promises.readFile, without checking isFile(). Thus a readable special file such as /dev/zero can pass the 500000-byte guard with size 0 and cause an unbounded read.

src/core/customRulesEngine.ts accepts gu flags and advances zero-length global matches using regex.lastIndex++, which can repeatedly return the same match when that increment enters an astral character's surrogate pair. The zero-length tests in src/core/__tests__/customRulesEngine.test.ts cover only ASCII inputs, and a bounded reproduction of /(?:)/gu against 😀 repeatedly returned index 0.

This duplicates C6's Unicode zero-length-match nontermination finding: src/core/customRulesEngine.ts preserves gu flags and uses lastIndex++ in the same matching loop. The defect is real, but this candidate identifies no separate issue or additional fix beyond C6.

StatisticsLoaderThread.getStatistics() passes dataManager.getNotes() directly into Statistics, whose constructor retains that list, while StatisticsExtension now reuses the cached Statistics when reopening the dialog. MonthChart.setFilter() queries those retained notes and StatisticsUtil.countWords(Note) reads their current text, whereas Statistics retains precomputed totals and maps, so editing a retained note can make the heatmap disagree with the cached aggregates without refreshing.

This duplicates C1: Statistics retains allNotes directly, and MonthChart.setFilter() recounts their text while StatisticsExtension reuses the cached aggregates. It identifies the same inconsistent-snapshot defect rather than an additional finding.

This duplicates C1's cache-consistency defect at the newly added reuse branch in StatisticsExtension. The cited loader, Statistics constructor, and MonthChart recounting path establish the same cause and consequence already covered by C1.

This duplicates C1, with more detailed citations to the same source path: StatisticsLoaderThread passes the notes into Statistics without copying, and MonthChart recalculates word counts when initialized or filtered. Its proposed snapshot or daily-aggregate fix addresses the same defect, not a separate issue.

The fullscreen branch in courses.$courseId.lessons.$lessonId.tsx adds max-h-[45vh] and overflow-hidden to the wrapper without constraining VideoPlayer itself. video-player.tsx still renders a full-width aspect-video container and full-height YouTube iframe, so on wide viewports the wrapper clips the video and its bottom playback controls rather than resizing them.

This duplicates C1: the fullscreen route's max-h-[45vh] overflow-hidden wrapper clips the unchanged aspect-video container in video-player.tsx. It identifies the same defect and requires the same correction, not a separate finding.

In lib/transcript.ts, stripVttTags uses only DOMParser.parseFromString(text, "text/html") and body.textContent, and parseVtt stores that result as cue.text for transcript display. WebVTT inline timestamps such as <00:00:01.000> are not HTML tags and remain literal text under HTML parsing, so this does not produce markup-free visible caption text.

This duplicates C5's parser defect: lib/transcript.ts passes cue payloads through HTML DOMParser without explicitly removing WebVTT inline timestamps. The different cited location does not identify an additional defect or require a separate fix.
